summary: The candidate verifies a narrow crash-avoidance fallback: compact target-verify graph capture is skipped for backends that do not advertise ragged-verify graph support. Triton-backed Qwen hybrid verification therefore remains eager and compact CUDA-graph execution is not fixed. The exact B300/CUDA 13.2 illegal memory access was not reproducible on the assigned AMD ROCm environment.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: unsupported compact capture entered warmup; five tests passed and the issue-specific test errored.
Candidate regression: six mock/control-flow tests passed.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-237c14d3ae6f/venv/bin/python - (independent capability, capture-boundary, and GPU numerical checks)
tests.what_was_measured: All four hybrid child-capability combinations, compact/non-compact capture continuation, and a HIP tensor result against an independent CPU reference.

gpu_execution.evidence: A numerical tensor operation executed on the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X and exactly matched a CPU reference. The candidate regression itself did not execute extend_attention_fwd or a hybrid model.

remaining_counterexamples: For a Triton-backed Qwen hybrid model, compact target verification still does not use a CUDA graph; the candidate deliberately routes it to eager execution.
The NVIDIA B300/CUDA 13.2 illegal memory access at batch size 20 and eight tokens per request was not reproduced or retested on matching hardware and weights.
The regression proves mocked capture/replay admission control only; it does not execute extend_attention_fwd or a hybrid full-attention/GatedDeltaNet model.
remaining_limitations: The assigned device is AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950 under ROCm 7.2, not NVIDIA B300/CUDA 13.2.
Required Qwen hybrid and DSpark weights were unavailable.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
